summary: Built 1935 by the CCC and Forest Service as a C-3 live-in cab in Sequoia NF; a Forest Service employee now lives in the tower; open to visitors when the gate is open.

facts.design: C-3 type 14 x 14 ft live-in cab with catwalk, on a short foundation

access.note: Visitors may go up when the gate is open; a sign on the gate may say whether the lookout is open. Roads to the base are typically open June to October.

visit.trail_note: Short hike up a dirt and gravel walkway; the brochure calls the climb moderate, including the walkway

events.note: Site probably first used as a lookout observation point around 1912, before the current cab
Current C-3 cab built by the CCC and Forest Service; materials packed in by mule
fire-lookouts.org says manned in 1936; the register says in service since 1935
June 1937 newspaper: lookout to be manned from June 10, visitors welcome; one mile from the road
Bea Rice and Helen King keeping watch since 1943, per a July 1951 newspaper item
July 1947 newspaper names two lookouts on Tobias, Helen King and Etha Rice; register lists 1947 as not in active service
Sunday Peak Lookout, considered a hazard, burned down by the government; Tobias had been chosen to replace it
Register says the observer had been in post since 1992

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935 date is for the current cab. The use of the peak around 1912 was an earlier lookout use. Fire-Lookouts.org and the 2025 brochure both give 1935 for the cab.

notes_for_editor: Coordinates and elevation disagree. The record (from the register) has 35.849955, -118.572367 and 8,218 ft (2,505 m). Fire-Lookouts.org gives 35.5101 N, 118.3421 W and 9,292 ft; peakbagging.com also says 9292 ft. The 1937 and 1946 newspapers give 8,200 and 8,550 ft. Left unchanged; a map check is needed. Staffing: the 2025 brochure says a Forest Service employee resides in the tower; Fire-Lookouts.org (undated) says it is no longer staffed, and in the same paragraph says it is currently staffed. The access level 'restricted' is my reading of the gate note; check current gate policy with the Forest Service before editing. 1947: the register says not in active service, but a July 1947 newspaper item names two lookouts on Tobias. 1936 (Fire-Lookouts.org) and 1937 (newspaper, 'will be manned June 10th') differ on when manning began. District: the register and Fire-Lookouts.org say Hot Springs RD; the 2025 brochure says Western Divide RD. The 1954 burning was Sunday Peak Lookout, not Tobias. The 1947 item names Etha Rice and the 1951 item names Bea Rice; the story keeps each name with its own date and source. The story now states the fire-lookouts.org staffing conflict in full (no longer staffed, and staffed 5 days a week in the same paragraph).
